findings.name: public.has_role executable to authenticated role
findings.resolution: Revoked EXECUTE from PUBLIC/authenticated; kept SECURITY DEFINER for RLS policies only.
findings.policy_or_query:
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.has_role(uuid, public.app_role) FROM PUBLIC, authenticated;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.has_role(uuid, public.app_role) TO service_role;
findings.details: SECURITY DEFINER functions executable by the `authenticated` role can be invoked with arbitrary arguments to probe role membership across users. The function is only needed inside RLS policies, which run as the policy owner regardless of caller EXECUTE privileges, so the client-facing EXECUTE grant was revoked.

findings.name: audit-fetch-page susceptible to SSRF
findings.resolution: Added DNS pre-resolution with private-range blocklist and canonical URL validation.
findings.details: Unrestricted server-side fetch allowed attackers to probe internal IP space (169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.0/8, ::1). The endpoint now enforces https, resolves DNS ahead of time, rejects private ranges and metadata endpoints, and caps response size.

findings.name: audit-deep-dive edge function missing auth
findings.resolution: Enforced JWT verification and admin role check inside the function handler.
findings.details: Endpoint calls a paid AI gateway. Public access allowed credit exhaustion attacks. Handler now requires a valid Supabase JWT and applies a 10/hour per-user rate limit.

findings.name: Internal host allowlist audit log readable by any authenticated user
findings.resolution: Replaced permissive SELECT policy (USING true) with admin-only policy using has_role(auth.uid(), 'admin').
findings.details: The internal allowlist audit log includes triage notes, decisions, and operator identifiers. A permissive USING (true) policy exposed those to every authenticated user. Restricted read access to admins via has_role() to preserve confidentiality of moderation activity.
